He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim l', it moves through themes of holiness, judgment and calls readers toward hope.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows holiness lived out in assyrian crisis, exile hope. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: The Lord Yahweh’s Spirit is on me, because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives and release to th
But you will be called Yahweh’s priests. Men will call you the servants of our God. You will eat the wealth of the nations. You will boast in their glory.
For as the earth produces its bud, and as the garden causes the things that are sown in it to spring up, so the Lord Yahweh will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations.

questions.question: What is happening in Isaiah 61?
questions.answer: In 11 verses, this chapter isaiah 61 (11 verses) continues the story of holiness. starting with 'the lord yahweh’s spirit is on me, because yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. he has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim l', it moves through themes of holiness, judgment and calls readers toward hope. The setting is assyrian crisis, exile hope, written to judah. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote Isaiah and why 61 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally isaiah son of amoz, addressed to judah around ~700 bc. This chapter fits the book's purpose as prophecy — its themes of holiness, judgment build on what came before.

questions.question: What does 'covenant' mean in this chapter?
questions.answer: Binding promise/agreement God makes with people. In this chapter, it appears in context of holiness. For a first-time reader: think of it as binding promise/agreement god makes with people, not just religious jargon.

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through holiness and judgment, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 10 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh! My soul will be joyful in my God, for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation. He has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bri...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about holiness. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
